leads.name: The Fountains Abbey Yews (Seven Sisters), Ancient Yew Group 773/774, Kitchen Bank
leads.status: HELD ON ACCESS, not delivered as verified (former rip_001)
leads.reason: Real and alive in 2024 per a blog, but access is unsettled and hard rule 10 forbids private land: Graham Wilkinson's 1997-98 West Riding yew survey (ancient-yew.org PDF) says 'The two surviving ancient trees lie to the SW on private land', a 2024 visitor says the plot sits beside a tenant farm, 'untended and fenced off' with a gate, while the Ancient Yew Group page lists access as public with National Trust responsibility. Needs the National Trust to say if the enclosure can be visited (not ATI, not Woodland Trust). Facts kept: AYG 773 ancient 5-7 m class, girth 663 cm at 30 cm; 774 ancient 4-5 m class, fallen with new growth, propped, mesh over a cavity (2009-2010 photos by Edwin Pretty); 171 lost; grid ref SE27206820 = 54.109011,-1.585388 (approximate, shared by the pair); survey 15 June 2002 (Tim Hills); Wilkinson 1998 GR 274683 and a moss-covered stump near the south wall of the Abbey, the old yew nearest the south wall gone. History: AYG says yews recorded almost from the 1132 founding; 1758 account 'seven yew trees ... of incredible size' (Lowe 1897), Lowe cites 1658 for 774; Britain Express 'only two of the original seven remain, protected by a fenced enclosure'; no source dates the living trees to 1132. Age left empty.

leads.name: Studley Royal wild cherry (Great British Trees, Tree Council 2002)
leads.reason: Alive but nearly crownless (NT: 'in decline', shed much of its crown); one source for position, no coordinate; walk step 3 puts it on the right just before the brow of the hill past a small crossroads, no pin in reach. Yorkshire Post (undated) says it still leafs each year. Needs a pin from a photo or reader; a superlative ('largest/oldest wild cherry in Britain') is the Tree Council/NT/Yorkshire Post wording only.

leads.name: Studley Royal pre-18th-century oak (walk stop D) and champion oak with cable bracing
leads.reason: NT names them on the ancient trees walk (oak right of the road past the cherry; champion oak with hole and cable bracing down the grass track); no coordinates or girth in reach, no pin.

leads.name: Old sweet chestnut at the crest of the hill (walk stop A, step 7), with a bench made from the neighbouring chestnut's branches
leads.reason: NT walk only; no coordinate or measurement. Chestnuts on that hillside planted about 1710 per NT.

leads.name: Studley Royal Water Garden yew (Ancient Yew Group 772)
leads.reason: 457 cm at ground, fluted bole, by a recently planted yew hedge near a lake, 2002 survey. Coordinates on the record are a map link of unstated axis order; inside paid water garden. Kept for a pin later.

leads.reason: Planning-dispute coverage (The Stray Ferret) says 150-200 years and ties it to the closed ATI; not an ancient tree and the age comes from ATI. Not researched further.
